attribution.note: Marcus's own post, in the authorial 'we'. He co-authored Hendrycks et al. The words 'current systems fall short' are his own assertion, not a quote of the paper.

semantics.note: The normalised proposition keeps both parts: the three named criteria are essential to AGI, and current systems fall short on them. It is a present-tense observation with no hedge.

contract.note: Using the paper he cites as the measure is a fair plain reading. The contract correctly flags that his paraphrase does not match the paper's CHC-domain framing. The result does not depend on that, because the paper reports both a large score gap and brittleness.

evidence.note: The paper's abstract (v3, Dec 2025) gives GPT-5 57% of the AGI bar, with critical deficits and a 'substantial gap'. This predates the post.
The full text calls current systems' generality brittle and points to profound weaknesses. This matches his point about robustness.

Nature opinion piece claiming human-level AI has arrived. It applies a Turing-style standard and gives no measurement under the Hendrycks framework, so it does not meet the contract's contradiction condition.

reviews.rationale: The framework he names scored GPT-5, a frontier model available before the post, at 57% with critical deficits. The paper also describes current generality as brittle. No evaluation in the packet shows a pre-post system near the bar. Models released after GPT-5 went unscored, but that does not create a contradiction. The Nature piece is a contrary opinion under a different standard.

attribution.note: Authorial statement in Marcus's own post, written in the co-authors' 'we'.

semantics.note: Revision 2 correctly restores 'have tried' and 'we see no evidence'. Both parts are firm observations.

contract.note: 'Original standards' and 'weakening' have no measure from the speaker. The contract uses Hendrycks et al. as a proxy for the standards and reads 'weakening' as less demanding than cognitive generality. Both are ordinary, reasonable readings, but the result does depend on them.

evidence.note: TechCrunch, via The Information, reports a profit-based AGI definition in the Microsoft–OpenAI agreement. That is a recent non-cognitive redefinition, and the report itself contrasts it with rigorous definitions.
The Hendrycks paper (Oct–Dec 2025) finds a substantial gap for GPT-5 against a broad human-level standard. This supports the claim that the demanding standard had not been met.
Contrary opinion that human-level AI is here, based on a Turing-style argument. It is not an evaluation against robust-generality criteria, and it arguably illustrates the redefinition he describes.

reviews.rationale: Part 1 holds: a documented profit-based AGI definition counts as a non-cognitive recasting of the term. Part 2 holds: the main broad evaluation before the post shows a large gap, and nothing in the packet shows a system meeting robust-generality criteria. The Nature comment is opinion under a different standard and does not meet the contradiction condition.

attribution.note: Authorial assertion in Marcus's post, under the heading 'Where current systems fall short'.

semantics.note: The proposition compresses the named standards (robustness, generalization under novelty, autonomous goal-directed behavior) into 'original AGI standards', but keeps the qualifier. 'Remain limited' is a weak, firm claim.

contract.note: The plain reading (large shortfall against humans on novel-environment and goal-discovery tests) is fair. Using March 2026 evaluations of Opus 4.6, a model current at the post, is reasonable for assessing the systems of that date. Given the size of the gap, the outcome does not depend on the threshold chosen.

evidence.note: ARC-AGI-3 launch: Claude Opus 4.6, current at the post, scored 0.25%. Humans solved all environments. Other models scored are post-dated and serve as corroboration only.
Describes the test design: no instructions or stated goals, so the agent must explore and plan. This shows relevance to the named standards but is not itself an outcome.
Organizer's description of ARC-AGI-3 (novel environments, acquiring goals on the fly). It establishes what the benchmark measures.
Opinion piece claiming human-level AI. It contains no measurement on the named standards, so it does not contradict.

reviews.rationale: The claim is weak ('remain limited'). Independent ARC-AGI-3 results show Claude Opus 4.6, a frontier system current at the post date, scoring 0.25% where humans score 100%, on a test of generalization to novel environments and goal acquisition. That is a large shortfall on the speaker's named standards. The only counter-item is an opinion piece without measurement.

attribution.note: Authorial assertion in Marcus's own post.

semantics.note: Three firm sub-claims are preserved. 'Depend heavily on human scaffolding' slightly compresses 'for task formulation, evaluation, and correction', but the meaning is kept.

contract.note: The plain readings are ordinary. However, 'struggle' has no threshold: a ~50% success rate on 14.5-hour tasks can be read either way. 'Lack persistent goals' has no measure, and agentic evaluations themselves use scaffolds. The result turns on these readings, which the speaker did not supply.

evidence.note: Secondary report of METR's Feb 2026 result: Opus 4.6 has a ~14.5h 50% time horizon on clean software tasks. This cuts against 'struggle with long-horizon reasoning'. The confidence interval is wide and the task suite is near saturation.
A custom human-built harness lifted Opus 4.6 from 0.25% to 97.1% on one ARC-AGI-3 environment. This shows heavy dependence on scaffolding, though for a single environment only.
Frontier models scored under 1% on ARC-AGI-3, which tests long-horizon planning with sparse feedback in novel settings. This supports 'struggle' outside well-specified tasks.
METR's own caveat (Sep 2026) that its tasks are cleaner than real work and that performance drops on messier tasks. It tempers e1 and falls outside the target period.

reviews.rationale: The scaffolding sub-claim has support: one harness took a near-zero score to 97% on one environment. The long-horizon sub-claim splits: ARC-AGI-3 supports it in novel environments, while METR's ~14.5h horizon on clean software tasks cuts against a flat 'struggle'. 'Lack persistent goals' has no measure in the packet and stays unresolved.
